title: Norwegian Fish Pudding
description: A traditional Norwegian dish featuring fish, gelatine, and butter, served on a salt block, this recipe is a unique and delicious way to enjoy fish, and is also ayurvedic-sattvic-friendly.
instructions: Rinse the cod fillets under cold water, pat dry with paper towels, and cut into small pieces.
Soak the gelatine leaves in cold water for about 5 minutes, until they become soft and pliable.
In a large skillet, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat, add the chopped onion, carrot, and celery, and cook until the vegetables are softened.
Add the cod pieces to the skillet, cook until they are opaque and flake easily with a fork.
Remove the skillet from the heat, stir in the soaked gelatine leaves, white pepper, and salt, until the gelatine is fully dissolved.
Stir in the heavy cream, and let the mixture cool to room temperature.
Pour the mixture into a heat-proof bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until set.
Preheat the salt block in the oven at 200 degrees Fahrenheit for about 30 minutes.
Remove the pudding from the refrigerator, scoop it onto the preheated salt block, and top with chopped parsley and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter.
Serve the pudding immediately, garnished with additional parsley if desired.
